transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I keep starting school projects and committee work with good intentions but I can’t seem to follow through and finish things on time, no matter how hard I try to stay on top of it. It's become a major issue recently with my increased workload as a teacher, and I'm seeking help at the urging of my wife and my department head.

Do you also have ongoing problems with inattention or restlessness in other parts of your life, such as losing things, being easily distracted, or feeling unable to sit still, or is the main issue just finishing tasks on time?

I don't really struggle with physical restlessness like being unable to sit still, but the mental distraction and losing things are huge issues for me. I'm constantly misplacing my grade book, USB drives, or papers, and I frequently zone out during meetings or when people are talking to me. I also find myself forgetting everyday responsibilities like replying to emails, paying bills, and keeping appointments.
Did these problems with distractibility, losing things, and forgetfulness start in childhood or the teen years, and were they present in more than one setting such as school, home, or work?

Yes, looking back, these issues definitely started during childhood. My primary school report cards always said I was bright but constantly daydreaming and losing homework, and my parents had to sit with me just to get simple tasks done. They've persisted ever since, affecting me through university and every job I've had.
Before age 12, did you have similar problems with inattention, forgetfulness, or losing things at home and at school, and did teachers or family members notice them?

Yes, definitely. In primary school, my teachers frequently wrote on my report cards that I was bright but constantly daydreaming, losing my homework, and forgetting instructions. At home, my parents had to sit with me every night just to get me to finish simple assignments because I kept spacing out.
Do you also have a long history of being very impulsive or physically restless, such as interrupting others, blurting out answers, fidgeting, or feeling driven to keep moving?

No, I've never really struggled with physical restlessness or impulsivity. I've always been more of a quiet daydreamer who spaces out, rather than someone who is fidgety, talkative, or constantly on the go. My issues have always been about losing focus rather than being hyperactive.
Have you ever had a pattern of being unusually restless, impulsive, interrupting others, or feeling unable to sit still, even if it was not severe?

No, I've never really experienced those symptoms at all, even mildly. I have never struggled with physical restlessness, impulsivity, or interrupting others. My difficulties have always been strictly focused on attention, daydreaming, and staying organized.
How much are these attention and organization problems affecting your work, home life, or relationships right now—for example, are they causing missed deadlines, mistakes, or conflicts?

They are having a huge impact both at work and at home. At school, my missed deadlines and inconsistency recently led to a critical mid-year review and have really damaged my professional reputation. At home, my wife is very frustrated because I'm constantly working late into the evening to catch up on things, leaving me unable to spend quality time with her as planned.
Just to confirm, have you ever had any significant problems with hyperactivity or impulsivity, such as fidgeting, interrupting others, blurting things out, or feeling unable to sit still?

No, I don't recall ever having significant issues with hyperactivity or impulsivity, like fidgeting, interrupting others, or feeling restless. My difficulties have always been much more about focus, daydreaming, and staying organized rather than physical restlessness.

Hyperactivity and impulsivity are repeatedly denied, making other ADHD presentations less likely. The provided candidate code F98.8 is the best match given the available options.
